react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on pyrimidine metabolism disruption as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR = 1.74e-10, fold-enrichment = 692.8) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 4.47e-6, rank 1) independently identified KEGG:hsa00240 as the top hit, while Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis confirmed the same pathway at p = 4.20e-4 with 13 of 14 pathway metabolites matched to input compounds. The four driver metabolites—2'-deoxyuridine, uridine 5'-monophosphate, 5,6-dihydrouracil, and N-carbamoyl-β-alanine—form a coherent catabolic trajectory: uridine monophosphate is reduced to dihydrouracil, which is ring-opened to N-carbamoyl-β-alanine, a known β-alanine precursor. Deoxyuridine enters the pathway from DNA/RNA turnover, consistent with nucleotide catabolism disruption. Deoxyribose 1-phosphate (RaMP rank 1 nucleotide catabolism) and CDP corroborate the nucleotide pool disturbance via Mummichog. The secondary beta-alanine metabolism hit (KEGG:hsa00410, p = 0.0024) is biologically coherent since N-carbamoyl-β-alanine feeds directly into this pathway. Methionine sulfoxide, spironolactone, and 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid did not contribute to pyrimidine hits and may represent treatment-specific off-target or unrelated metabolic effects. The cross-paradigm consensus on pyrimidine catabolism is robust across ORA (RaMP, MetaboAnalystR) and m/z network (Mummichog) methods.
